name: Julia DeGraw
subject: Take Action to Protect Oregon’s State Forests!
body:
Help Us Keep Oregon State Forest Protections On Track! | | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/75971941/446291528/241075653?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI5MzllYzU2LWJjYTUtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyM2YzNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=RZRRrWkT9X3V0Qi_3TzoBwTLeICl2_m0Yg41vFKwZ_E=&emci=a34e78d1-b6a5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&emdi=b939ec56-bca5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&ceid=2107230) Dear Peter,

Though the road is long and winding, we're getting ever closer to historic protections for salmon streams, wildlife habitat, mature forests, and clean water in our Western State Forests.

Thanks to you and the power of your voice demanding the strongest Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) possible, this past July, the Department of Forestry (ODF) began implementing many of the protections in the State Forest HCP that we’ve been supporting for the past two years. It’s clear that ODF is anticipating and preparing for the final federal approval of the HCP in late 2024.

That’s great news, but we haven’t won yet and with the Board of Forestry meeting on January 3rd it’s imperative that [**we speak up for strong habitat protections**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/75971942/446291529/241075653?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI5MzllYzU2LWJjYTUtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyM2YzNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=RZRRrWkT9X3V0Qi_3TzoBwTLeICl2_m0Yg41vFKwZ_E=&emci=a34e78d1-b6a5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&emdi=b939ec56-bca5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&ceid=2107230)—louder than the logging industry that still wants ODF to scrap this plan completely. Earlier this month, the Department of Forestry issued new logging estimates for the 70-year lifespan of the HCP. Under the revised estimates, logging will be reduced to more sustainable levels compared to the past 20 years of excessive logging of state forests. This is needed to restore balanced management on our state forests. But the logging industry and their political allies are using this information to try and derail the HCP process.

[**Can you speak up today in support of passing the HCP as it stands: a plan that strikes the best possible balance between logging and the many other critical values that Western State Forests provide to people and wildlife?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/75971943/446291540/241075653?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI5MzllYzU2LWJjYTUtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyM2YzNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=RZRRrWkT9X3V0Qi_3TzoBwTLeICl2_m0Yg41vFKwZ_E=&emci=a34e78d1-b6a5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&emdi=b939ec56-bca5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&ceid=2107230) This won’t be the last time we’ll need to speak up for strong habitat protections and conservation. The HCP is still at least one year away from federal approval. We’ll need to keep the pressure high or risk losing the progress we’ve made. The current HCP is a big gain for conserving crucial habitat for threatened and endangered species (such as salmon, and the marbled murrelet), and there are additional ways that we can further improve management of state forests:

* We must provide larger protective buffers on headwater streams. A recent peer-reviewed study on the Trask River supports HCP Alternative 3 with larger protective buffers on small streams; and
* We need to modernize the antiquated law that couples state forest timber revenue with funding for the counties: counties deserve more stable funding for local services.

We know there's more work to do, and we’re working hard to gain more ground in the coming months. [**But right now, the Board of Forestry needs to hear loud and clear that we want them to keep the HCP on track.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/75971944/446291553/241075653?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI5MzllYzU2LWJjYTUtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyM2YzNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=RZRRrWkT9X3V0Qi_3TzoBwTLeICl2_m0Yg41vFKwZ_E=&emci=a34e78d1-b6a5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&emdi=b939ec56-bca5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&ceid=2107230)

The logging industry won’t be satisfied until our state forests are managed like private industrial forests. And delay and derailment tactics are its specialty. For the sake of our remaining mature state forests and the clean drinking water and healthy fish and wildlife habitat they provide, let's keep this legacy plan on track. [**Please tell the Board of Forestry to finalize a strong HCP without delay!**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/75971945/446291567/241075653?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI5MzllYzU2LWJjYTUtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyM2YzNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=RZRRrWkT9X3V0Qi_3TzoBwTLeICl2_m0Yg41vFKwZ_E=&emci=a34e78d1-b6a5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&emdi=b939ec56-bca5-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&ceid=2107230)

Thank you, Julia DeGraw
Coalition Director, OLCV |

subject: Weaponized government came after me.
body:
The hardest part was seeing your family and friends worry about you when your face is on TV and are cameras are outside your door.. | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us1.campaign-archive.com/?e=17913c7d6d&u=10a708d6740341bfdc2a52a46&id=bc30e46a20)
---
| | |
---
| | | Friends,

My name is Jeffrey Clark.

You may have seen me in the news this past year. The headlines weren’t pretty, in fact, they were downright ugly. The mainstream media slandered, maligned and dragged my name through the mud.

**Why? Because I was one of the “co-conspirators" along with President Trump who faced phony charges as part of the 2020 election. **

Thankfully, Russ Vought and the Center for Renewing America (CRA) had my back. From the day the phony charges were announced to the media circus that met us outside the Fulton County Jail, **CRA stood by me through the worst of it.** Providing support, refuge, and a paycheck.

And they've promised to support me in 2024 as I face these phony charges, but we need your help.

**[That’s why I'm asking you to support the Center for Renewing America in your 2023 giving](https://americanrestorationcenter.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=10a708d6740341bfdc2a52a46&id=7d26d4fcf0&e=17913c7d6d).**
---
| [ ](https://americanrestorationcenter.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=10a708d6740341bfdc2a52a46&id=1149e2e3f4&e=17913c7d6d)
---
| (My mugshot at the Fulton County Jail)
---
| I’ve been asked what it’s like to face the wrath of our weaponized government. The hardest part was seeing your family and friends worry about you when your face is on TV, cameras are outside your doors, and legal troubles are piling up.

_Frankly, this is what happens when you serve President Trump honorably and refuse to stop fighting for the integrity of our elections_. They come after you with all they have. Just last year, DOJ agents raided my home in the pre-dawn hours on the same false premises.

That’s why I was overwhelmed at [the support](https://americanrestorationcenter.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=10a708d6740341bfdc2a52a46&id=48580457e2&e=17913c7d6d) that poured in from patriots just like you when my colleague Russ Vought and the team here asked you to “[Stand by Jeff](https://americanrestorationcenter.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=10a708d6740341bfdc2a52a46&id=af3008b7e5&e=17913c7d6d).”
---
| [ ](https://americanrestorationcenter.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=10a708d6740341bfdc2a52a46&id=b5551d1bdd&e=17913c7d6d)
---
| But the real fight has just begun. The charges have been made against me in the court of law and I intend to fight them tooth and nail with Russ Vought and the CRA team beside me in the coming months.

I know what I'm asking of you. Things can be tight around the end of the year, but there is no organization more worthy of your support than the Center for Renewing America.

[And If you want to stand with me, there’s no better way than to give generously to the Center for Renewing America](https://americanrestorationcenter.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=10a708d6740341bfdc2a52a46&id=c5adb4fe46&e=17913c7d6d).

They are fighting 24/7 to put God, Community, and Country back in the center of American life.
---
| Sincerely,

Jeffrey Clark
Senior Fellow and Director of Litigation
Center for Renewing America

From the day the phony charges were announced to the media circus that met us outside the Fulton County Jail, CRA stood by me through the worst of it. Providing support, refuge, and a paycheck. And they've promised to support me in 2024 as I face these phony charges, but we need your help. . | | (My mugshot at the Fulton County Jail) | I’ve been asked what it’s like to face the wrath of our weaponized government. The hardest part was seeing your family and friends worry about you when your face is on TV, cameras are outside your doors, and legal troubles are piling up. Frankly, this is what happens when you serve President Trump honorably and refuse to stop fighting for the integrity of our elections. They come after you with all they have. Just last year, DOJ agents raided my home in the pre-dawn hours on the same false premises. That’s why I was overwhelmed at that poured in from patriots just like you when my colleague Russ Vought and the team here asked you to “.” | | But the real fight has just begun. The charges have been made against me in the court of law and I intend to fight them tooth and nail with Russ Vought and the CRA team beside me in the coming months. I know what I'm asking of you. Things can be tight around the end of the year, but there is no organization more worthy of your support than the Center for Renewing America. . They are fighting 24/7 to put God, Community, and Country back in the center of American life. | Sincerely, Jeffrey Clark Senior Fellow and Director of Litigation Center for Renewing America | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Copyright © 2023 Center for Renewing America, All rights reserved. | For his entire career, my dad has worked hard to make a difference — a real difference — in people’s lives.
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=4894%2E5257348%2EF6Frc1)
Hey Derek, it’s Lexi, Adam’s daughter!
[](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=dec2023_abs_em.181qVM&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC90_20231228_PM1_V1_S1&email=&t=4&akid=4894%2E5257348%2EF6Frc1)
As a young woman living in the United States, I am keenly aware of the challenges my generation faces. The cost of renting apartments keeps going up and buying a house seems out of reach for so many families.
We’ve seen the far-right Supreme Court strip us of reproductive rights and block President Biden’s plan to cancel student loan debt.
Our climate is getting worse. Too many Americans lack access to clean air and clean drinking water.
And one entire political party seems more focused on supporting Donald Trump than American democracy.
It’s tough out here — and as a young person, sometimes I feel like politicians don’t really care about people in my generation.
**But my dad is different. And I’m not just saying that because he’s my dad.**
For his entire career, my dad has worked hard to make a difference — a real difference — in people’s lives.
Whether it was getting new textbooks for schools in California as a State Senator or securing funding for affordable housing in Congress, he listens to people’s problems and concerns and _does something about them._
It’s why he supports Medicare for All. It’s why he supports the Green New Deal. It’s why he supports reforming the Supreme Court, protecting our democracy, and keeping Trump the hell away from the White House.
**I know my dad will be a fantastic U.S. Senator for all Californians — young, old, and everywhere in between.**

| **Missouri's regular legislative session gets underway Jan. 3**
The Missouri General Assembly’s 2024 regular legislative session gets underway Jan. 3 with election-year politics expected to dominate proceedings with several lawmakers making bids for higher office and others maneuvering to strengthen re-election bids. At least 10 sitting lawmakers are vying for statewide office, while a number of House members seek promotion to the Senate. The session ends May 17.

Although until recent years it was standard for the legislature to grant final passage between 100 and 175 non-appropriations bills during a given session, infighting among majority Republicans has resulted in fewer than 50 non-appropriations bills being sent to the governor in each of the last three years. Those disputes, resulting from hardline Senate conservatives holding up legislation in a largely unsuccessful effort to leverage passage of polices that are priorities for them but opposed by most lawmakers, isn’t expected to abate in the coming session.

Republicans are again expected to focus on “culture war” issues such as prohibiting Missouri schools from teaching about racism in American history and its continuing modern day impact; banning public institutions and private businesses from promoting diversity, equity and inclusion; further restricting the rights of transgender Missourians; and allowing firearms on public transit and in churches.

The majority party also is likely to make a last-ditch effort at making it harder for Missourians to use the initiative petition process to enact laws or amend the state constitution independently of lawmakers. Republicans want new restrictions in hopes of thwarting an initiative drive seeking to enshrine protections for abortion and other reproductive rights in the state constitution. If it gathers enough signatures, the abortion measure would go on the November 2024 statewide ballot. Any restrictions on the initiative process likewise would require voter approval

Democrats will advocate for relaxing Missouri’s draconian laws that outlaw abortion in nearly all instances, including rape or incest, and also seek to reduce crime by restoring the common-sense gun safety laws Republicans have repealed over the last 15 years. Democrats also will push for tax relief for working families by eliminating sales taxes on food, period products and diapers. Republicans, by contrast, are expected to seek income tax cuts for corporations and wealthy individuals in addition to those already enacted in recent years that have led to flat net state general revenue collections.

Republicans outnumber Democrats 111-51, with one vacant seat last held by a Democrat, in the House of Representatives and hold a 23-11 advantage in the Senate. Although the GOP holds veto-proof majorities in both chambers, Gov. Mike Parson, a Republican, has yet to have one of his vetoes overridden. Even though the House has voted to override on several different measures, the override efforts have always died in the Senate.

| **Missouri's minimum wage increasing to $12.30 an hour**
Missouri’s standard minimum wage is set to increase to $12.30 an hour effective Jan. 1 – a bump of 30 cents an hour, according to the Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations.

A 2018 ballot measure Missouri voters approved with 62.3 percent support gradually raised the state’s minimum wage from $7.85 an hour to $12 an hour over five scheduled increases starting in 2019 and ending in 2023. As of 2024, the measure requires the wage to be adjusted annually – upward or downward – based on changes in the Consumer Price Index. That adjustment is resulting in the 30-cent bump about to take effect.

The increases imposed by the 2018 law only apply to private sector employees. However, competition for workers has forced most government employers in Missouri to keep pace with private sector wages. Missouri’s state minimum wage is well above the federal minimum wage of $7.85 an hour.

| **Couple who threatened protesters won't get firearms back**
A St. Louis couple who pleaded guilty to misdemeanor charges for brandishing firearms at anti-police brutality protesters as they passed by the couple’s home won’t get their weapons back, even though Gov. Mike Parson subsequently pardoned them for their crimes, the Missouri Court of Appeals Eastern District ruled on Dec. 26.

The June 2020 incident in which Mark and Patricia McCloskey respectively pointed a Colt AR-15 rifle and a Bryco .380 pistol at protesters walking by their house on the way to the nearby home of then-St. Louis Mayor Lyda Krewson generated national controversy after the St. Louis Post-Dispatch published photographs of the couple menacingly clutching their weapons.

The McCloskeys originally were charged with felonies but in June 2021 pleaded guilty to misdemeanors and, as part of their plea agreement, forfeited ownership of the weapons involved. Their prosecution was denounced in conservative political circles, and Parson, a Republican, pardoned the couple about six weeks later.

Days after the pardon, Mark McCloskey asked a court to order the firearms returned, even though the couple had consented to forfeiting ownership as part of their guilty pleas. A St. Louis judge rejected McCloskey’s request, finding that the pardon didn’t entitle them to have the weapons back. McCloskey appealed, but the three-judge appellate panel agreed with the lower court’s ruling and, citing a 1976 Missouri Supreme Court precedent, concluded McCloskey remains factually guilty of the crime he committed, despite the pardon.

“While we agree that the pardon restored all of his rights forfeited by the conviction and removed any legal disqualification, disadvantage or impediment, Missouri law is unequivocal that a gubernatorial pardon obliterates the fact of the _conviction_ , not the fact of _guilt_ ,” Judge James Dowd wrote. “Thus, McCloskey’s guilty plea, for which he obtained the benefit of the State dismissing a felony charge punishable by jail time, survived the pardon and importantly, with respect to the issue at hand in this replevin action, triggered the guns’ forfeiture. Therefore, since McCloskey’s guilt remains, it follows that he is not entitled to the return of the weapons.”

McCloskey could further appeal to the state Supreme Court. The case is _Mark T. McCloskey v. State of Missouri, et al._

| **HELP FOR SMALL BUSINESS AND NON- PROFITS **
The U.S. Small Business Administration approved Missouri’s request for assistance through the federal agency’s disaster loan program. This move makes low-interest disaster loans available to small businesses and private non-profits severely impacted by the Coronavirus (COVID-19).

SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loans offer up to $2 million in assistance for each affected small business or non-profit. These loans can provide vital economic support to small businesses to help overcome the temporary loss of revenue they are experiencing.

Applicants will be able to apply online, receive additional disaster assistance information and [download applications](https://robertsforstl.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6e3f7ee3b541518ea63c7e773&id=a908e1f02c&e=a088917f89). Applicants may also call SBA’s Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955 or email [disastercustomerservice@sba.gov](mailto:disastercustomerservice@sba.gov) for more information on SBA disaster assistance.

Capitol Ave., Rm 329 Jefferson City, MO 65101 (573) 751-4415 Steve.Roberts@senate.mo.gov | | | | | | | | | | | | Missouri's regular legislative session gets underway Jan. 3 The Missouri General Assembly’s 2024 regular legislative session gets underway Jan. 3 with election-year politics expected to dominate proceedings with several lawmakers making bids for higher office and others maneuvering to strengthen re-election bids. At least 10 sitting lawmakers are vying for statewide office, while a number of House members seek promotion to the Senate. The session ends May 17. Although until recent years it was standard for the legislature to grant final passage between 100 and 175 non-appropriations bills during a given session, infighting among majority Republicans has resulted in fewer than 50 non-appropriations bills being sent to the governor in each of the last three years. Those disputes, resulting from hardline Senate conservatives holding up legislation in a largely unsuccessful effort to leverage passage of polices that are priorities for them but opposed by most lawmakers, isn’t expected to abate in the coming session. Republicans are again expected to focus on “culture war” issues such as prohibiting Missouri schools from teaching about racism in American history and its continuing modern day impact; banning public institutions and private businesses from promoting diversity, equity and inclusion; further restricting the rights of transgender Missourians; and allowing firearms on public transit and in churches. The majority party also is likely to make a last-ditch effort at making it harder for Missourians to use the initiative petition process to enact laws or amend the state constitution independently of lawmakers. Republicans want new restrictions in hopes of thwarting an initiative drive seeking to enshrine protections for abortion and other reproductive rights in the state constitution. If it gathers enough signatures, the abortion measure would go on the November 2024 statewide ballot. Any restrictions on the initiative process likewise would require voter approval Democrats will advocate for relaxing Missouri’s draconian laws that outlaw abortion in nearly all instances, including rape or incest, and also seek to reduce crime by restoring the common-sense gun safety laws Republicans have repealed over the last 15 years. Democrats also will push for tax relief for working families by eliminating sales taxes on food, period products and diapers. Republicans, by contrast, are expected to seek income tax cuts for corporations and wealthy individuals in addition to those already enacted in recent years that have led to flat net state general revenue collections. Republicans outnumber Democrats 111-51, with one vacant seat last held by a Democrat, in the House of Representatives and hold a 23-11 advantage in the Senate. Although the GOP holds veto-proof majorities in both chambers, Gov. Mike Parson, a Republican, has yet to have one of his vetoes overridden. Even though the House has voted to override on several different measures, the override efforts have always died in the Senate. | | | | Missouri's minimum wage increasing to $12.30 an hour Missouri’s standard minimum wage is set to increase to $12.30 an hour effective Jan. 1 – a bump of 30 cents an hour, according to the Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations. A 2018 ballot measure Missouri voters approved with 62.3 percent support gradually raised the state’s minimum wage from $7.85 an hour to $12 an hour over five scheduled increases starting in 2019 and ending in 2023. As of 2024, the measure requires the wage to be adjusted annually – upward or downward – based on changes in the Consumer Price Index. That adjustment is resulting in the 30-cent bump about to take effect. The increases imposed by the 2018 law only apply to private sector employees. However, competition for workers has forced most government employers in Missouri to keep pace with private sector wages. Missouri’s state minimum wage is well above the federal minimum wage of $7.85 an hour. | | | | Couple who threatened protesters won't get firearms back A St. Louis couple who pleaded guilty to misdemeanor charges for brandishing firearms at anti-police brutality protesters as they passed by the couple’s home won’t get their weapons back, even though Gov. Mike Parson subsequently pardoned them for their crimes, the Missouri Court of Appeals Eastern District ruled on Dec. 26. The June 2020 incident in which Mark and Patricia McCloskey respectively pointed a Colt AR-15 rifle and a Bryco .380 pistol at protesters walking by their house on the way to the nearby home of then-St. Louis Mayor Lyda Krewson generated national controversy after the St. Louis Post-Dispatch published photographs of the couple menacingly clutching their weapons. The McCloskeys originally were charged with felonies but in June 2021 pleaded guilty to misdemeanors and, as part of their plea agreement, forfeited ownership of the weapons involved. Their prosecution was denounced in conservative political circles, and Parson, a Republican, pardoned the couple about six weeks later. Days after the pardon, Mark McCloskey asked a court to order the firearms returned, even though the couple had consented to forfeiting ownership as part of their guilty pleas. A St. Louis judge rejected McCloskey’s request, finding that the pardon didn’t entitle them to have the weapons back. McCloskey appealed, but the three-judge appellate panel agreed with the lower court’s ruling and, citing a 1976 Missouri Supreme Court precedent, concluded McCloskey remains factually guilty of the crime he committed, despite the pardon. “While we agree that the pardon restored all of his rights forfeited by the conviction and removed any legal disqualification, disadvantage or impediment, Missouri law is unequivocal that a gubernatorial pardon obliterates the fact of the conviction , not the fact of guilt ,” Judge James Dowd wrote. “Thus, McCloskey’s guilty plea, for which he obtained the benefit of the State dismissing a felony charge punishable by jail time, survived the pardon and importantly, with respect to the issue at hand in this replevin action, triggered the guns’ forfeiture. Therefore, since McCloskey’s guilt remains, it follows that he is not entitled to the return of the weapons.” McCloskey could further appeal to the state Supreme Court. The case is Mark T. McCloskey v. # [BREAKING: Maine kicks Trump off 2024 ballot! Thank the official who made this happen](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tf6b3049d-f4af-4462-992a-0be233302b09/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

| | | _BREAKING: Maine has now joined Colorado in removing Trump from the ballot! **[Please join us in thanking the official who made this happen ](https://default.salsalabs.org/T8931cb7e-e909-48ec-968e-09fb2e493750/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**_ Maine's top election official -- Secretary of State Shenna Bellows -- has removed Donald Trump from the state's 2024 ballot, citing the 14th Amendment's "insurrectionist ban." "I do not reach this conclusion lightly," [Bellows wrote](https://default.salsalabs.org/T3eb5ee98-2a4e-412d-b4ee-2ba295a93dc6/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9). "Democracy is sacred ... I am mindful that no Secretary of State has ever deprived a presidential candidate of ballot access based on Section Three of the Fourteenth Amendment. I am also mindful, however, that no presidential candidate has ever before engaged in insurrection." **The Constitution makes it clear: If you engage in insurrection, you can't be president. ** Bellows was right to remove Trump from the ballot, and other officials and courts -- including the Supreme Court -- need to do the same. [**Sign on, and join us in thanking Bellows and Maine for taking this essential step.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tf5ead0b6-9320-4673-ace1-fd946ff602b0/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

Hi there — I know it’s the busy holiday season, but I wanted to bump the email below.Right now, political analysts, the media, and even *Republicans* themselves are saying the same thing: Control of the U.S. House will come down to California.

That’s why we are working to boost our Forever Organizing program by opening a regional office earlier than ever in a part of the state with one of the most competitive, tossup districts in the country.

If we flip the district, this could quite literally be the seat that flips the entire U.S. House from Republican to Democratic control.

That’s why it’s so important that we hit our $12,500 fundraising goal. Would you please consider making a donation? I’ve pulled a custom link below and hope to see your contribution come in:

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cdp-dec23?refcode=20231228_FR_90DO_FieldOfficeFwd&amount=20.24 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cdp-dec23?refcode=20231228_FR_90DO_FieldOfficeFwd&amount=20.24]- Camille

Camille Alcala (she/her/hers)

Hi team — Did you know that there are enough competitive seats in California alone to flip the U.S. House from red to blue?
Here at California Democratic Party HQ, we are CONSTANTLY analyzing the data and making decisions on where to deploy resources to strategically flip seats blue.
One seat we are targeting is California’s 41st Congressional District which is rated a TOSSUP .

I'm reaching out to you today as a fellow warrior in the fight for a brighter, more equitable future. Like Alexandria, I beat millions of racist, sexist, Republican-funded attacks because of the people-powered movement we have all worked so tirelessly to build.

We've beaten the odds before, and with your continued support, we can and we will do it again!
[Consider splitting a donation between our campaigns today! Whether it's a small or large amount, every contribution brings us a step closer to a future where every person is heard, valued, seen and supported.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20231228-summer.l_NYjp&refcode=em20231228-5548-P_FND_RES_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=5548%2E2526796%2EIqpdkB)

In solidarity,
Summer Lee

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftteran?refcode=X_122823_Iwouldrather [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftteran?refcode=X_122823_Iwouldrather]
Hi Peter, it’s Raquel.
Fundraising for a grassroots campaign like ours is tough, especially this time of year.
Sometimes, I joke with the team that after being on the phone nonstop for hours and spending the weekends approving our emails and texts, I would rather get a root canal than ask for another donation.
But here’s why I do it: I realize I’m not asking this for myself, but so we can all go to Congress together. We deserve so much better. Working Arizonans deserve better pay; women deserve to have control over their own bodies; and immigrants, just like the rest of us, deserve a shot at a better life.

Kat Cammack is serving her second term representing the people of Northeastern Florida in Congress. She won the seat on a conservative platform of growing jobs, securing our southern border, standing up for law enforcement, defending our Second Amendment, promoting fiscal responsibility, and defending life.
Congresswoman Cammack sits on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and House Committee on Agriculture, where she is the only Florida Republican serving the Sunshine State's farmers, ranchers, and producers. She was also appointed to the Select Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government.
Kat and her husband Matt, who is a firefighter, paramedic, and SWAT medic, proudly call Gainesville, Florida home.

Vivek is a first-generation American. Growing up in the Cincinnati area, he often recounts the sage advice he received from his father that "If you're going to stand out, then you might as well be outstanding." He went on to graduate summa cum laude in Biology from Harvard in 2007 and received his J.D. degree from Yale Law School in 2013, worked at a hedge fund, then started a pharmaceutical company, Roivant Sciences, where his team developed five drugs that went on to become FDA-approved.

In 2022, he founded Strive Asset Management, an Ohio-based firm, that takes direct aim at asset managers like BlackRock, State Street, Vanguard and others for their fiduciary breach of duty to maximize the wealth of their clients for Wokeism. Friend,
It's getting colder in South Texas, a reminder that some families in our community face the bitter cold even within their homes.
As a lawyer for over 20 years, I've helped people in our community have a safer and better place to live , taking on cases that others might shy away from to fight big companies looking to take advantage of us.
I have always believed in standing up for those who need it the most, and my commitment to this principle has only grown stronger over the years.
One story close to my heart involves a family whose home, damaged by Hurricane Sandy, left them with a **wide hole in the roof** that they covered with plastic bags, leaving them exposed to the elements. Through hard work and litigation, we secured justice and provided them a new home.
Our neighbors and community members deserve a safe and warm place to call home, which is why I want to continue to fight for our district in Congress.
Our region, especially the colonias in South Texas, faces unique challenges that demand a strong voice in Congress and who understands their unique challenges and is committed to finding real solutions.
I am committed to being this advocate, but I need your help.
Friend, as December unfolds and the temperatures drop, we must work hard to make sure no one in Texas faces the winter without a secure roof over their head. Will you help me win this crucial seat by donating to my grassroots campaign today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vgonzalez-email?refcode=20231220_em_fr_b1_VG_initial]
DONATE TODAY [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vgonzalez-email?refcode=20231220_em_fr_b1_VG_initial]
In unity,
Congressman Vicente Gonzalez
Vicente Gonzalez, a life-long Democrat, is a candidate for Texas’ 34th U.S. Congressional District.
From humble beginnings, Vicente was raised in a military family. Through hard work and pure ganas, Vicente aimed to make something of himself. His mother stressed to him over and over again that education was the key that will open doors of opportunities. Vicente made the decision to get his life back on track by going back to school to get his GED, working and attending classes at community college, and earning his college degree alongside other military families at the Embry Riddle Aeronautical University on the Corpus Christi Naval Air Station. Friend, I'm incredibly proud to call Florida home. From our welcoming, diverse communities to the unique natural beauty of the Everglades, the Sunshine State is a home to be proud of.
_But I am _not_ proud to call Rick Scott my senator._

Peter,

Right now, we’re just three days away from the end of 2023 and a few
months out from the Democratic primaries that can determine whether or not
our progressive incumbents remain in Congress.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20231228-2.jg0lVn&refcode=em20231228-32558&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1001&akid=32558%2E1203867%2E8A4bch ]We’re running out of time to raise the resources needed to protect and
re-elect the Squad next year: will you rush a grassroots donation of ANY
amount to help us reach our $75,000 goal by midnight on New Year’s Eve?

With AIPAC planning to spend an unprecedented $100,000,000 in 2024, our
young, diverse, working-class, progressive movement will face our biggest
challenge yet in the months ahead.

In April, Summer Lee will go up against a Democratic challenger in
Pennsylvania, where she narrowly won her last primary by just 1 point and
faced $4 million in attacks from AIPAC.

career politician George Latimer in a New York primary Politico is calling
“one of the country’s top battlegrounds.” An AIPAC donor is even
encouraging Republican voters to switch parties in order to vote in this
Democratic primary and oust Jamaal.

prosecutor Wesley Bell, who pulled out of the U.S. Senate race to run for

were offered tens of millions of dollars from AIPAC to drop out of their
race to run against Rashida.

And on August 13, Ilhan Omar will once again face her former primary
opponent Don Samuels, who lost to her by only 2 percent in 2022.

Geoff Simpson

With AIPAC planning to spend an unprecedented $100,000,000 in 2024, our young, diverse, working-class, progressive movement will face our biggest challenge yet in the months ahead. In April, Summer Lee will go up against a Democratic challenger in Pennsylvania, where she narrowly won her last primary by just 1 point and faced $4 million in attacks from AIPAC. In June, Jamaal Bowman will face AIPAC’s hand-picked moderate, white, career politician George Latimer in a New York primary Politico is calling “one of the country’s top battlegrounds.” An AIPAC donor is even encouraging Republican voters to switch parties in order to vote in this Democratic primary and oust Jamaal. In early August, Rashida Tlaib and Cori Bush will be on the Democratic primary ballots in Michigan and Missouri. Cori is being challenged by prosecutor Wesley Bell, who pulled out of the U.S. Senate race to run for Cori’s seat once he saw the backlash she received for leading the call for a ceasefire in Gaza. Meanwhile, multiple U.S. Senate candidates say they were offered tens of millions of dollars from AIPAC to drop out of their race to run against Rashida. And on August 13, Ilhan Omar will once again face her former primary opponent Don Samuels, who lost to her by only 2 percent in 2022. AIPAC and its affiliates like Democratic Majority for Israel — who are bankrolled by the same right-wing millionaires and billionaires who support Trump — are once again using their dark money and influence to infiltrate the Democratic primaries in an attempt to get rid of the Squad for good. We can’t let them succeed. | Peter,

As our climate crisis worsens each year, the threat of wildfires looms larger over Washington each year. Too often, we’ve seen communities devastated by fast-burning fires or choked in the smoke from burning forests and grasslands. With a growing threat to life and property, Hilary Franz knew she needed to take action to rethink the way our state responds to these crises.

Under Hilary’s leadership, Washington has emerged as a national leader in wildfire prevention. She led the charge to increase funding for mitigation and prevention, so our frontline workers have the resources they need on the job.

Hilary's work as an advocate for our emergency workers is why groups like the _Washington Fire Chiefs, Gig Harbor Firefighters Local 3390, South Kitsap Professional Firefighters IAFF Local 2876, East Pierce County Firefighters Local 3520, and West Pierce Fire Fighters IAFF Local 1488_ have lined up behind her campaign for Washington's 6th Congressional District.

Our heroes stand with Hilary as the most pro-labor lands commissioner in our state’s history, and we can expect nothing less from her in Congress. But to get there, Hilary needs your help.

clean_body: Under Hilary’s leadership, Washington has emerged as a national leader in wildfire prevention. | = | Peter, As our climate crisis worsens each year, the threat of wildfires looms larger over Washington each year. Too often, we’ve seen communities devastated by fast-burning fires or choked in the smoke from burning forests and grasslands. With a growing threat to life and property, Hilary Franz knew she needed to take action to rethink the way our state responds to these crises. Under Hilary’s leadership, Washington has emerged as a national leader in wildfire prevention. She led the charge to increase funding for mitigation and prevention, so our frontline workers have the resources they need on the job. Hilary's work as an advocate for our emergency workers is why groups like the Washington Fire Chiefs, Gig Harbor Firefighters Local 3390, South Kitsap Professional Firefighters IAFF Local 2876, East Pierce County Firefighters Local 3520, and West Pierce Fire Fighters IAFF Local 1488 have lined up behind her campaign for Washington's 6th Congressional District. **About Jim Jordan:** Leading the fight to hold Washington accountable.

**
In Washington, Jim Jordan is focused on his oversight role, helping lead investigations into federal agencies

In Congress, Jim Jordan continued to fight for fiscal responsibility,and he offered the only balanced budget of any member of the House or Senate.

As a state legislator, he took on the powerful special interests and the leaders from both political parties who wanted to put Ohio on an unsustainable path of higher taxes and spending.

I’ve always been able to count on my Professor Warren for support, and I hope I can count on you too.

Hey, Katie Porter here. Elizabeth let me know I could reach out, because with the way things are looking in the California Senate primary right now, this is a make-or-break moment for my time in office. California’s unique jungle primary system means the top two vote-getters, regardless of party, advance to the general. Two recent polls show me in third place — trailing two points behind Republican celebrity Steve Garvey. I’m still very much in this race to win it — because I believe that working people in California and across the country deserve a Senator who will stand up to powerful corporations and fight for affordable housing, a Green New Deal, and Medicare for All. [**The silver lining of this situation is that nearly 30% of voters are undecided about who they’ll support in this race. But I need your support ASAP to raise as much as we can before our end-of-quarter deadline on Sunday so we can reach these undecided or swayable voters in time for our March primary. Can you please chip in right now to make sure I can keep fighting in office?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1057?t=8&akid=1873%2E4032634%2E2AyUo6)

Dave Reichert here.

I'm trying to flip the Governor's seat in Washington from Blue to Red. **[I want you to know WHO I am, and WHY I am running for Governor of Washington. So, I figured I'd tell you a little bit of my story. Here goes.](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=1ae3ca63ee1c419c850d008d45751037&_e=tmynN42u0VxTxrx-9PNXyxeLDCfmAHPVAdBEFqCXOEgNUnepKHQaEja0kt0uNVesGJxqtRTVfibciqE93OjWvtvOpvimhuzZWF-f4qTMmmtlTZpHHgpb4QCAspOaoYoGXcNNRFvAKVwUTK2_mUdREEmqzsUwrTuuNcyr-d3iWd2HmgpozF0xHWIjnIOlJDWMm5lbXDLqEWQb_WwFuij4Feh66vEd3tVinirX217F5F_VGlwdOLneBIQ5T4jm_kXLROlgCZ-DHF2ewrjJ4fpDhmg3363RiwsSYgtPP2j_0Yv4rLlOLyqYs30GFRJ_Hsjss3Zls6edZ9FN90x_2yKUK3jgeATYErlxjZ1i1xEH22LaAX8jF38m4Irb-owJb9-nEYu8hN68PRVVSw1s9e8RO6oinY30WwsfU5Q3WQynxHs%3D)**

I grew up right here in Washington, and graduated from Kent Meridian High School. I attended Concordia Lutheran College in Portland, where I played football and basketball - and most importantly, where I met my wife **Julie**. We have three wonderful children and six grandchildren. Julie and I are truly blessed.

In 1972, while serving in the **US Air Force Reserves** , I joined the King County Sheriff's office and found a calling in law enforcement. Keeping the citizens of **King County safe** was one of the most fulfilling occupations I have ever had.

I'm honored to have served as the lead detective on the **Green River Killer 's** case, putting a monster who terrorized our community behind bars. Knowing I was playing even a small part in keeping my community, my neighbors, and my family safe was something I cherished for years in Law Enforcement.

I later authored a book called **" Chasing the Devil"**, with all proceeds going to a charity that helped babies born with drug addiction. I truly believe in protecting the most vulnerable among us, and keeping our communities SAFE. I then went on to serve Washington's **8th District in Congress** from 2005 to 2019, fighting for common sense solutions to the problems facing us as a nation. **Friend, I don 't tell you all of this to boast or brag; I tell you this because I want you to understand that I am determined to serve the people of Washington. I believe Washington needs a dedicated and committed servant to protect the vulnerable, help small businesses, and keep people safe. **
I believe Washington needs **SERVANT LEADERSHIP** , and I'm ready to be that servant. Too often, the government gets too big, too overbearing, and pits families, generations, and communities against one another. I believe the government should be responsible, open, and responsive.

**[If you're willing to make a contribution to my campaign, please do so here. I need all the help I can get, in order to get across the finish line in November of 2024, and get to work helping YOU. ](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=1ae3ca63ee1c419c850d008d45751037&_e=tmynN42u0VxTxrx-9PNXyxeLDCfmAHPVAdBEFqCXOEgNUnepKHQaEja0kt0uNVesGJxqtRTVfibciqE93OjWvtvOpvimhuzZWF-f4qTMmmtlTZpHHgpb4QCAspOaoYoGXcNNRFvAKVwUTK2_mUdREEmqzsUwrTuuNcyr-d3iWd2HmgpozF0xHWIjnIOlJDWMm5lbXDLqEWQb_WwFuij4Feh66vEd3tVinirX217F5F_VGlwdOLneBIQ5T4jm_kXLROlgCZ-DHF2ewrjJ4fpDhk_wp8nLwtIYKCRRiMoWjrHEohympNfJUtHBr0nYYvHtF4g1MYMklXpl3CuTbsjAWo72kmLmvOfEgpSd_1FWj1Efxde8LfoPJtSgx-xI9agdZ1lRMXsiKNx9t1yMiTwAfk3pESQuXPzEwfexWW8vptc%3D)**

Thanks,

Dave Reichert
Republican for Governor

Hi Friend,
As we stand on the cusp of 2024, it's a momentous occasion to reflect on the incredible journey we've shared throughout the past twelve months. Each chapter, from the highs to the lows, has provided us with valuable lessons and insights that will guide us into the future.
In 2023, the Supreme Court made some awful historic decisions, from striking down student loan forgiveness and affirmative action, President Trump was indicted in four separate cases, heartbreaking mass shootings, and environmental challenges such as record heat worldwide, wildfires, and diminishing Antarctic ice. Congress went missing without a Speaker and wars continued abroad.
Amidst these challenges, positive beacons illuminated our path. We witnessed historic investments in renewable energy, helping foster a sustainable future. Labor agreements with SAG-AFTRA, WGA, and UAW marked collaborative efforts for fair working conditions. Cultural icons like Elton John bid farewell to the stage, while Taylor Swift continued to captivate audiences globally. Barbie graced the theaters with a powerful message, and NASA's announcement of astronauts for the first moon trip in over 50 years reignited our sense of wonder. George Santos is out of Congress.
At home in Minnesota, almost all no-knock warrants were banned, a new state flag will be ushered in, and starting in January employees will not be allowed to ask about prior pay to help decrease the gender and racial pay disparities.
It’s been a crazy year, with some positive highs and awful lows. Invest $24 in our movement to help turn the page. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dean24-email?refcode=12.28.2023.Review&amount=24]
So much has transpired, and as we navigate the complexities of our world, let's focus on carrying the positive momentum of 2023 into the new year. Together, we can shape a future that reflects our shared values and aspirations.
To a better 2024,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP50/1/103532/images/Signature.png]
- Dean

**The Pro-RCV Group Hired a “SPY” & “LIED” “STOLE” & Lost Anyway!!!****Imagine a scene straight out of a spy novel: The Pro-Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) group, in a twist of espionage, allegedly hired a 'spy' to infiltrate and disrupt the grassroots movement against RCV, and Stole 2 of our Petition Books, which we filed a Police Report on. But the plot thickens. In a bold move, the Pro-RCV group and their attorney attempted to persuade the State of Alaska to shut down our constitutional right to petition the government. Fortunately, the State stood firm and declined their request.****This isn’t fiction. It’s the reality of our ongoing battle to uphold our Republic in Alaska. We emerged victorious in this clash, but the war is far from over.****Our determination is stronger than ever, reflected in the over 34,000 signatures we've gathered so far, a number that continues to grow each day.****Our focus now turns to Anchorage Districts 14 through 18, where our efforts need to intensify. Below, you'll find an up-to-date chart detailing our progress and the work that lies ahead. Your support and participation are crucial. Join us in this fight to preserve our right to petition and shape the future of voting in Alaska.**

#### **PSA:**
#### **We submitted a formal complaint to APOC (Alaska Political Office Commission) concerning the actions of the Pro-RCV group in Alaska. While they have accused us of breaching various State Campaign Finance Laws, we assert that this group should also adhere to the same rules and regulations. Contrary to their portrayal, this organization is not grassroots and receives substantial funding from outside of Alaska. Our objective is to hold them responsible for their apparent hypocrisy and their attempts to intimidate and tarnish the image of Alaskans, their organizations, and families. Their efforts to suppress our movement against ranked choice voting should not go unnoticed, and they must answer for potentially breaking the same laws they accuse us of. It's concerning that these well-informed political activists, who have benefited from massive out-of-state donations for their ranked choice voting agenda and campaign finance law changes, manipulate the system to their advantage, expecting regular citizens to falter and then overwhelm them with financial and legal burdens. We trust that the State of Alaska will ensure that these laws are applied uniformly, calling this Pro-RCV group to account for any disregard of Alaskan laws and norms.**
#### **Please see the full 111 page complaint when it is made public by the news and APOC. All of this information is public information.**
